text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned knee pain after increased physical activity; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and if there was a specific injury or sudden movement when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the specific type of pain you feel—is it sharp, aching, or does it feel like a "pop" occurred when it started? Additionally, is the knee visibly swollen, or do you feel any instability, like the knee "giving way," when you walk?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the location of your pain (medial tibia) and the history of repetitive pivoting in volleyball, I suspect you may have a tibial stress fracture or severe Osgood-Schlatter disease. Can you tell me if pressing directly on the bony prominence below your kneecap causes sharp pain? Also, have you noticed any redness or warmth around that specific area?

text: RESULTS: X-Ray_Knee: No fracture, dislocation, or appreciable joint effusion. MRI_Knee: Optional; considered if clinical suspicion persists despite negative initial workup.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), currently managed with oral contraceptive pills. Social history: Has recently joined a volleyball team.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, recent injuries, swelling or discoloration of the knee, or previous similar complaints. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming; the absence of fever, swelling, or discoloration makes an infectious process or acute hematoma less likely. To definitively confirm a stress fracture versus soft tissue inflammation, can you tell me if the pain is worst when you bear weight or when you press directly on the tibial tubercle?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)
